newsitem.title: USA: Chirac to press Clinton on Romania joining NATO.
newsitem.headline: Chirac to press Clinton on Romania joining NATO.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Friday he would tell U.S. President Bill Clinton that Romania should be among the first wave of nations invited to join the NATO Western security alliance.

Germany, reflecting European doubts about limiting the new entrants to three as Washington wants, said it had not decided whether to press for Romania and Slovenia to join Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic in entering NATO.
The United States surprised its allies last week by saying its firm position was that only three former Warsaw Pact states should join the pact in the first wave.

"I think it is in the interest of Europe and also of Romania that it be part of the first set of countries admitted into an expanded NATO," Chirac told reporters through an interpreter before a meeting with Clinton.
"I certainly will be presenting this viewpoint," he added.

German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said after a meeting with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Friday that the Bonn government had not yet agreed on its position for NATO talks scheduled to take place in early July.
"We have not yet set the position of the federal government," Kinkel told reporters. "For us three, four or five (new members) would be thinkable."
Leaders of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation will meet in Madrid July 8-9 to formally invite the countries selected to begin membership negotiations.
The United States has set 1999, the alliance's 50th anniversary, as the target date for their admission.
Leaders of the most powerful Western industrial states are in Denver for the annual summit of the Group of Seven starting Friday evening.
